title: Expose identical calibration means with different concurrent memory outputs
statement: The source constructs two smooth passive waveforms of equal total pi/2 area, one swapping before and one after the same middle source pulse. Their three endpoint calibration means agree, yet the retained outputs are a nontrivially excited state and vacuum. A common pulse shape or a separate path-error contract is required.

requires: Identified canonical retained a and fresh thermal b_j, independent of the complete incoming state
Known prescribed passive waveforms, bounded common source envelope and invariant first-mean region; no departed-mode return
provides: A source-specific counterexample to endpoint-only waveform transfer
assumptions: This is missing path information, not a physical limit on concurrent control
costs: One fresh thermal mode per execution contact; actual calibration starts, controls, timing, detector state and collected-output storage
A declared narrow 1000-contact visibility plan requires about 3.838e15 hypothetical native-vacuum starts; no such measurements occurred
contract.units: Dimensionless probabilities/Bell loss/half-diamond error as explicitly stated; source calls, resets, memory and control gates are separate costs.
contract.obstruction: Identical endpoint areas do not identify time-ordered nonlinear operations.

evidence.quote: ### Equal endpoint area does not identify concurrent memory dynamics
evidence.range_scope: Governing producer statement; retain the complete source contract and review scope.

body: Physical canonical ports, phases, pulse shape, thermal freshness and the same retained input are supplied. The source-only unanchored kernel theorem does not identify these ports. Equal endpoint pulse area can give different retained states when chronology differs. Model-comparison error is not device error, task success or independent reset; collector uncertainty and extra memory remain separately paid. Read the exact supporting statement and its applicable conditions. Producer review status is preserved; no new scientific audit or producer-code execution was performed for this insertion.
